acceptanceCriteria: Novo componente step1-compose-message.tsx: textarea pro corpo do texto (com inserção de token de variável {{1}}/nome de campo, mesmo estilo de token que o template já usa), upload de mídia opcional (reaproveita o componente de upload já usado pra header de template)

Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Text length is validated against captionMaxLength — the only per-provider text-length capability the channel contract exposes (lib/channels/types.ts); broadcast-core.ts (US-005) already treats this same text as the media caption when media is attached, so one provider-driven limit correctly governs both cases. Media type/size validated against mediaKinds and min(provider.maxMediaBytes, the chat-media bucket's own 16 MB file_size_limit) — never advertises a limit the upload itself can't honor. Browser-verified end-to-end with a throwaway QA account + a Telegram connection: step1-compose-message.tsx renders (not the template picker), 'Insert variable' inserts {{1}}, Avançar is disabled with empty content, typing text enables it, exceeding captionMaxLength (1024 for Telegram) shows the specific over-limit message and blocks Avançar, a valid image uploads to chat-media and previews, and a 17 MB file is rejected client-side with the exact 16 MB bucket-cap message (no wrong channel name). Also verified the WhatsApp/template regression path: picking a whatsapp_cloud connection at step 0 still renders step1-choose-template.tsx unchanged.

userStories.notes: use-broadcast-sending.ts's per-batch POST to /api/whatsapp/broadcast now carries connection_id plus conditional content (template OR message_text/message_media_url), and no longer filters recipients by contact.phone before sending — a non-template channel resolves its target by contact_id -> contact_identities server-side (loadRecipientIdentities, exported from broadcast-core.ts), matching a phoneless-but-eligible Telegram contact instead of dropping it. Client<->server result correlation switched from phone-keyed to contact_id-keyed (phone can be empty/non-unique for a non-template channel). new/page.tsx's step-4 gate is now `(template || messageText)` (was `template` only); Step4ScheduleSend/handleSaveDraft generalized the same way (template optional, messageText/messageMediaUrl persisted when there's no template) so the newly-reachable free-message step 4 doesn't crash or misbehave. Browser-verified END TO END (not just to step 4, all the way through clicking 'Enviar broadcast') with a throwaway QA account: (1) WhatsApp/template regression — unchanged UI copy at every step, broadcast persisted with template_name and connection_id, delivery attempt reached the real whatsapp_cloud provider and failed only at 'WhatsApp connection has no access token' (no real Meta credentials exist in this dev environment for ANY story in this PRD); (2) Telegram/free-message — step 4 now renders (previously a dead end), summary shows the composed message text and '—' for Idioma, confirm dialog uses the new template-free confirmDescMessage copy, broadcast persisted with message_text and connection_id (template_name null), and delivery reached the real telegram provider, resolved the phoneless contact's target via contact_identities (not phone), and failed only at 'Telegram connection has no bot token' — proving identity-based target resolution and conditional-content dispatch both work; the only unverifiable piece is the final external hop to Meta/Telegram's live API, which needs real, human-owned credentials this dev environment doesn't have (same limitation every prior browser check in this PRD hit for WhatsApp, now also true for Telegram since the account's real bot connection is explicitly off-limits per progress.txt). All seeded QA rows deleted afterwards, verified 0 remain.
